questions.stem: Biofuels such as ethanol are sometimes described as 'carbon neutral'. What does this mean?

options.text: They contain no carbon atoms in their molecules
The CO₂ released when burned equals the CO₂ absorbed by the plants used to make the fuel
They produce no gases when burned
They are made entirely from recycled carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Carbon neutral means the net CO₂ emission is theoretically zero. The plants used to make biofuels absorb CO₂ from the atmosphere during photosynthesis. When the biofuel is burned, the same amount of CO₂ is released. However, in practice, energy used for farming and processing means biofuels are not completely carbon neutral.
